unruled:clcw.spouse_screen.reason: WIDE only; both findings refuse cases the worksheet computes correctly.

findings.evidence: First limb has no loss condition; a filer with no 2024 loss is refused though the tool computes zero carryover (i1040sd p. 10). Safe.
Filer who had the whole joint loss is refused though the full carryover is deductible (i1040sd p. 10). Safe.

unruled:dependent.divorced_rule.reason: One defect: a custodial parent who signed the release can read the question as not applying to them and the tool then lets them claim the child for the CTC/ODC; two WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 20: 'If conditions (1) through (4) apply, only the noncustodial parent can claim the child for purposes of the child tax credit and credit for other dependents'. A custodial parent who signed Form 8332 who answers no gets dependent.qualifying_child = true (forms/2025/dependent.yaml: residency/age/relationship tests only), so the CTC/ODC is claimed on both parents' returns. dependent.other_claimant is not a reliable backstop (the other parent fails residency on its face).
Ordinary custodial parent with no release answers yes and is refused; the tool computes the residency case. Safe.
Release holder failing the support/custody conditions is refused; tool would compute non-qualifying. Safe.

unruled:dependent.married.reason: One defect (low): a dependent who died during 2025 while married, whose surviving spouse files a joint return including them, can be answered no to both this screen and dependent.joint_return; two WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: Married non-joint filer refused on qualifying_child/qualifying_relative where i1040gi p. 21 lets the flow continue. Safe (and needed for eic_child, i1040gi p. 44).
Refund-only joint filer refused though dependent.joint_return computes the exception. Safe.

i1040gi p. 21: 'If the person is married and files a joint return, you can't claim that person as your dependent.' The example covers only the case where this person's spouse died; the sibling input dependent.joint_return ('Is this person filing a joint return for 2025...') carries the same ambiguity and computes rather than refuses, so a no to both lets the dependency/CTC compute for a person on a joint return.
Filer who already claimed the 2024 maximum is refused though line 9b is zero (i2441 p. 4, Line 9b). Safe.

unruled:f4952.alternative_allocation.reason: No defect: the two NARROW findings (line 5 investment expenses) are covered by f4952.unsupported, which gates the same four lines; the UNCLEARs either err wide or misread 'alternative allocation'.

findings.evidence: f4952.unsupported asks 'any deductible investment expense other than interest (for example depreciation or depletion ... or investment expenses on a Schedule K-1)' and gates f4952.line2, election, line5 and required (forms/2025/f4952.yaml).
Same: other deductible investment expenses (the Who Must File exception) are screened by f4952.unsupported on f4952.required.
The doubtful reading (any line 4g election counts) produces yes and a refusal of a default-allocation case the tool computes. Safe direction only.

f4952 p. 4 Note: any shift ('treat less of the amount on line 4e as attributable to line 4g', entering 'Elec.') is an alternative to the default; a filer deliberately making that entry is electing 'an alternative allocation' and the question names that election. No plausible truthful no.

unruled:f5695.construction_later.reason: No defect: WIDE accepted; installation completed in 2026 is excluded by the cost inputs' own definition; 'reconstruction' is the IRS's undefined term.

findings.evidence: Reconstructed home first used in 2025 may be answered yes and refused; tool's costs would be correct. Safe.

The amount inputs f5695.line1-line5a, battery_cost (interview/questions-2025.yaml help) say 'A cost counts in 2025 when the original installation is completed' (i5695 p. 1, Costs), so costs completed in 2026 are not entered; the screen does not need to carry this.

i5695 p. 1 itself does not define reconstruction; the screen repeats the IRS term. A renovation of an occupied home answered no falls back on the installation-completed rule, which is the ordinary rule.

unruled:f8959.unsupported.reason: No defect: SE income that reaches Schedule SE but not through this tool's Schedule C path is refused by person.se_screen (and K-1/Schedule F by scope.schedule1); territory W-2s other than 499R-2 are WIDE.

findings.evidence: person.se_screen (forms/2025/person.yaml) asks about partnership SE (K-1 box 14 code A), other SE income not on Schedule C, farm income, optional methods, church/clergy income, Forms 4137/8919, and refuses person.se_line2 -> person.se_line6 -> f8959.line8 (sum_over person.se_line6). A filer with K-1 or Schedule F income is also refused by scope.schedule1.
W-2AS/CM/GU/VI use boxes 5 and 6 (i8959 p. 1) and would compute; refusing them is safe.

unruled:household.credit_disallowed.reason: WIDE only; the UNCLEAR's doubtful reading also errs wide.

findings.evidence: Recertified EIC (i1040gi p. 43 exception) refused. Safe.
No-child EIC after a child-only disallowance (i1040gi p. 43) refused. Safe.
CTC recertified for 2024 (i1040gi p. 39) refused. Safe.
One answer refuses both credit families. Safe.
Reading 'reduced' as an ordinary phase-out gives yes (refusal); the no reading is the correct one (i1040s8812 p. 2). Only the safe direction is at risk.

unruled:refund.not_2024.reason: One defect: the second limb asks only about a late estimated payment, but Pub. 525's pro rata rule (which the refusal itself cites) applies to any 2024 tax paid in 2025, e.g. an extension or balance-due payment; WIDE accepted; 'refunds' is defined by the preceding amount input.

findings.evidence: p525 p. 24, Recovery for 2 or more years: 'If you receive a refund or other recovery that is for amounts you paid in 2 or more separate years, you must allocate, on a pro rata basis...'. A 2024 refund partly from an April 2025 extension payment is answered no; refund.taxable runs the i1040gi worksheet on the whole refund and Schedule A line 5a keeps the whole 2025 payment (Example 28 reduces it).
Non-itemizer for 2024 with a January 2025 estimate refused though the tool's zero is right. Safe (amb.2025.refund_exceptions chose to ask item 5 of every refund).
Other-year refund for a year without itemizing refused. Safe.

'These refunds' refers to the preceding amount input refund.line1 (forms/2025/refund.yaml: 'State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets ... including any part you chose to apply to your 2025 estimated ... tax and any part offset against a debt'), which the reviewer did not see.
Non-electing combat-pay recipient refused on lines whose amount would be zero (i1040gi p. 42; i2441 pp. 4-5). Safe.
Recipient never sent to the Earned Income Worksheet refused on line 1b. Safe.

unruled:s8812.puerto_rico.reason: No defect: Puerto Rico withholding of a non-resident is caught by f8959.unsupported (derived refusal of line 21, verified by eval); residency-term doubts can only under-claim the ACTC.

findings.evidence: A Form 499R-2/W-2PR holder answers yes to f8959.unsupported ('Medicare wages on a wage statement from a U.S. territory (such as Form 499R-2/W-2PR)'), which refuses f8959.line19 -> s8812.amt_ws4 -> s8812.line21 -> clwb_7 and Part II-B. Eval of fixtures stage4.base with f8959.unsupported=true: s8812.amt_ws4 = refusal (gate f8959.unsupported).
Resident refused where Part II-B cannot change the result (f1040s8812 p. 2). Safe.

The screen uses the form's own term ('If you are a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico, go to line 21'). A wrong no can only lower the credit: line 26 is 'the larger of line 20 or line 25' and CLW B line 11 is zero off the Puerto Rico path, so no overclaim results.
Same: IRS term of art, same direction argument.

unruled:sa.excluded_income.reason: No defect: the five NARROW Schedule A items are screened by sa.unsupported and sa.charity_limited, which gate the same lines; the WIDE findings are accepted; bare form numbers are a presentation point.

findings.evidence: sa.unsupported asks 'a foreign tax or generation-skipping tax deduction' and gates sa.line6.
sa.unsupported asks 'mortgage interest or points not on Form 1098' and gates sa.line8b, sa.line8c.
sa.charity_limited asks 'carried over from a prior year' and gates sa.line13.
sa.unsupported asks 'Any casualty or theft loss' and gates sa.line15.
sa.unsupported asks 'a deduction from the Schedule A line 16 list other than gambling losses' and gates sa.line16.
Form 4563/Puerto Rico filer refused at EIC Step 1 q. 3 (i1040gi p. 40 names only Form 2555). Safe.
Same on Form 2441 lines 4, 5, 18, 19 (i2441 p. 4). Safe.
Same on Form 8962 Worksheet 1-1 line 3 (i8962 p. 8). Safe.
SALT at or below the cap refused (i1040sca p. 7). Safe.

The exclusions cannot be claimed without the forms; a Form 2555 exclusion is also Schedule 1 line 8d, refused by s1.line8_other ('the foreign earned income or housing exclusion from Form 2555 (8d)'), and foreign wages not on a W-2 by scope.other_income. Naming the income would help but nothing unsupported computes.

unruled:sales.special.reason: One defect: shares of a physically backed precious-metals trust are strictly 'an interest in a ... trust holding' collectibles, but a holder of exchange-traded shares can reasonably answer no; the two WIDE findings are accepted.

findings.evidence: S corporation/trust interest holding only section 1250 property or QSB stock refused (i1040sd pp. 11-12 look-throughs). Safe.
Short-term entity interest refused. Safe.

i1040sd p. 11: 'Collectibles include ... metals (such as gold, silver, and platinum bullion)' and line 18 includes gain from 'an interest in a partnership, S corporation, or trust held for more than 1 year and attributable to unrealized appreciation of collectibles'. A long-term sale of gold-trust ETF shares on Form 1099-B answered no is computed as ordinary long-term gain at 0/15/20% instead of through the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet.

unruled:scope.other_line16.reason: One defect: Form 8615 is named only by number, so a child who must file it can answer no and be taxed at their own rates; passive Schedule C income and Form 2555 are refused elsewhere; WIDE and elective Schedule J accepted.

findings.evidence: A Schedule C business without material participation is refused by sc.passive -> sc.screened on sc.line1 (forms/2025/sc.yaml), and scope.other_income asks 'income or loss from a passive activity', refusing f1040.line8.
Form 2555 is Schedule 1 line 8d, named in s1.line8_other, which refuses s1.line9 -> f1040.line8 -> AGI -> taxable income -> line 16.
Form 8621 with no line 16e tax refused (i1040gi p. 34). Safe.

i1040gi p. 36: 'You must file Form 8615 if you meet all of the following conditions. 1. You had more than $2,700 of unearned income ... 3. You were either: a. Under age 18 ...'. No other input tests these conditions (the age/support/parent inputs in person.yaml serve only Form 8863 line 7). A 16-year-old filer with $10,000 of dividends who answers no gets f1040.line16 at their own rates.

Schedule J is an optional election (i1040gi p. 36 'your tax may be less if you choose'); a no computes the ordinary tax correctly. A Schedule D/Form 4952 filer reading 'filing' as yes is refused: WIDE, safe.

unruled:scope.schedule1.reason: One low defect: 'clergy income' is not defined, so a member of a religious order without a vow of poverty or a Christian Science practitioner paid on Form W-2 can answer no; the other NARROW findings are refused by sibling or derived gates; WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: Passive Schedule C business refused by sc.passive -> sc.screened on sc.line1; scope.other_income also asks 'income or loss from a passive activity'.
s1a.line5_calc is also gated by s1.sc_1a, counting Schedules C with sc.tips_ot ('qualified tips you received in the course of this business').

s1a.line14b_calc is gated by s1.sc_1a (sc.tips_ot asks about 'qualified overtime compensation reported to you on Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC'); outside Schedule C, a 1099-MISC box 3 amount entered on line 8z as 'other' is refused by oi8z.figured.

A section 1256 dealer answers yes to sd.other_forms ('Count section 1256 contracts', Form 6781) and to person.se_screen; every amount the Earned Income Worksheet feeds (ACTC line 27 via the tax limit, EIC via AGI) is then a derived refusal.

i1040gi p. 43, Clergy: 'The following instructions apply to ministers, members of religious orders who have not taken a vow of poverty, and Christian Science practitioners.' person.se_screen names all three but is asked only with a Schedule C; a W-2-only member of a religious order who answers no gets eic.step5_line1 from line 1z (no Worksheet B) and no SE tax on the ministerial earnings.
Church wages under $108.28 refused (i1040gi p. 42). Safe.
Clergy with an approved Form 4361 and W-2 only refused. Safe.
